official.deadline_note: Two-step schedule: step 1 pre-proposals closed 12/05/2026 at 12:00 CEST; step 2 detailed proposals are due 18/11/2026 at 12:00 CET. Only coordinators whose pre-proposal was recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different participating countries and who received the M-ERA.NET invitation may deposit in step 2. Partners requesting ANR aid must additionally deposit their detailed proposal on the ANR submission site, with the exact link and deadline communicated later by email.
official.application_cycle: M-ERA.NET Call 2026, 2027 edition for the ANR
official.status_note: The ANR call page shows the call as 'Ouvert - 2027'; the M-ERA.NET call page states the Call 2026 is currently in its full-proposal submission phase, with the pre-proposal evaluation completed and 116 research groups invited to submit a full proposal by 18 November 2026.
official.funding_period: per partner, project grant over up to 36 months
benefits: The ANR allocates no aid below 15 000 EUR per partner requesting its aid.
For a non-coordinating partner requesting ANR aid, the aid requested must not exceed 180 000 EUR.
For a coordinating partner requesting ANR aid, the aid requested must not exceed 250 000 EUR.
The total aid requested for a project with several ANR partners must not exceed 350 000 EUR.

An optional 20 000 EUR supplement per project is available for network-development activities, on a commitment to draft and submit, after the M-ERA.NET project, an international collaborative research proposal under the calls of the next European Framework Programme (FP10); this raises the ceilings cited above to 200 000, 270 000 and 370 000 EUR respectively.
Only the eligible costs of the partners that have requested ANR aid are financed; the applicable funding rate and cost types are set by the ANR Financial Regulation (eligible costs sheet no. 3).
eligibility: A pre-proposal or proposal must correspond to one and only one scientific collaboration theme defined in the call.
Maximum project duration is 3 years (36 months).

Minimum consortium of 3 partners requesting funding from a funding agency listed in Annex 3 of the call text and eligible for that funding, from at least three different countries, of which at least two are EU Member States or Horizon Europe associated countries participating in the M-ERA.NET Call 2026.
The coordinator must request funding from one of the agencies participating in the Call 2026 and be eligible there.
To be invited to submit a detailed proposal in step 2, the pre-proposal must be recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different countries participating in the Call 2026.
Each partner must meet its own funding agency's national or regional criteria, including its TRL requirements, and must be selected by that agency to receive funding.

ANR-eligible themes only: 1. Materials for energy storage and distribution systems; 2. Materials for energy conversion; 4. Innovative functional materials with designed architectures; 6. Next-generation materials for electronics. Partners in consortia positioned on theme 3 (innovative surfaces, coatings and interfaces) or theme 5 (materials addressing environmental challenges) are not eligible for ANR aid.

The end-of-project TRL must not exceed 5 for a partner funded by the ANR, on pain of ineligibility, and work by partners requesting ANR aid must necessarily be positioned either in the 'fundamental research' segment or in the first 'applied research' segment.

Partners, legal or natural persons, subject to European Union sanctions are excluded from the call; the ANR declares ineligible any partner requesting its aid that is associated, within the submitted project, with partners covered by a sanction measure. As of publication this concerns in particular partners from Russia and Belarus, and partners from territories of Ukraine escaping the control of the Ukrainian government.

A project proposal may not be similar in whole or in part to another proposal submitted to any ANR call under evaluation or funded by the ANR; similarity is established when the projects describe identical main objectives or result from a simple adaptation.
A researcher may request ANR aid (as partner, coordinator or co-coordinator) for only one proposal in the 2026/27 M-ERA.NET call.
requirements: Pre-proposals and detailed proposals, written in English, must be deposited by the project coordinator on the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission site.
Use of the templates available on the M-ERA.NET site is mandatory; any unauthorised modification, in particular exceeding the page limit, may render the proposal ineligible.
A pre-proposal with one or more partners requesting ANR aid must clearly indicate the topic studied and the TRL levels of the tasks of each French partner in the consortium.

The detailed proposal must be the duly completed detailed-proposal form in English and must include Annex 1 describing the partner profiles together with the CVs of all consortium participants, also in English.

Partners requesting ANR aid invited to step 2 must additionally deposit their detailed proposal on the ANR submission site, with information identical to the central deposit; the exact link and deadline are communicated later by email.

The scientific lead (responsable scientifique) formally commits that their hierarchy (administrative and financial services and persons legally entitled to represent the managing institution) has approved the submission and that the information has been communicated to them.

Where genetic resources are used, all participants must respect the Nagoya Protocol obligations, and beneficiaries under the access-and-benefit-sharing regulation must provide the Due Diligence Declaration receipt by the date of the final payment.

Before any ANR project deposit, applicants should approach their institution's defence and security officer or PPST services to verify the project's eligibility conditions; projects with foreign public or private partners are subject to SHFDS/MESR opinion, and a negative opinion prevents selection.

Beneficiaries commit to immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit of the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL, a FAIR approach to research data, and free-licence release and Software Heritage archiving of software.
documents: Pre-proposal form (step 1), in English, on the mandatory M-ERA.NET template (step closed 12/05/2026 at 12:00 CEST).

Detailed proposal form (step 2), in English, on the mandatory M-ERA.NET template, presenting the project as a whole and describing all its parts and each partner's contributions, due 18/11/2026 at 12:00 CET.
Annex 1 to the detailed proposal (mandatory), also in English, describing the partner profiles and containing the CVs of all participants in the consortium.

Parallel deposit of the detailed proposal on the ANR submission site for partners requesting ANR aid, providing all the information requested on the site, with information identical to the central deposit.
Consortium agreement (accord de consortium), mandatory except where the call provides otherwise, under the conditions set in the ANR Financial Regulation (sheet no. 4).
Data Management Plan (plan de gestion des donnees, PGD) within 6 months of the scientific start of the project, per the ANR aid award terms.
Intermediate and final progress reports, transmitted by the French partners to the ANR via the monitoring platform and by the coordinator to the M-ERA.NET follow-up team.
Formulaire 'Declaration relative aux activites economiques des Partenaires d'un projet ANR', where the applicable funding rate and cost types need to be established.
selection_criteria: Evaluation and selection are centralised at M-ERA.NET level and take place in two steps: step 1 central evaluation of pre-proposals by independent international experts convened by the M-ERA.NET Call Secretariat, with invitations to step 2 issued in ranking order and taking account of the participating agencies' budget capacity; step 2 central evaluation of detailed proposals by the same secretariat.

Proposals are ranked on the evaluation results and selection follows the ranking; the list of projects recommended for funding is drawn up by the group of participating funders taking account of their respective budget capacities, and the final funding decision is taken individually by the funders concerned.

ANR horizontal objectives: projects must show significant French participation (in coordination or in charge of a substantial part of the work), generate significant opening and diversification of French collaboration networks, and be ambitious with a clear intention of continuity and evolution of the collaboration.
During discussions to separate projects of similar scientific quality within the funder group, projects involving a wider and/or more diverse consortium may be favoured.
coverage: ANR aid of at least 15 000 EUR per partner requesting ANR aid, with the requested amount not exceeding 180 000 EUR for a non-coordinating partner and 250 000 EUR for a coordinating partner.
A total ANR aid cap of 350 000 EUR for a project with several ANR partners.

An optional additional 20 000 EUR per project for network-development activities, on a commitment to draft and submit, after the M-ERA.NET project, a collaborative international research proposal to calls of the next EU Framework Programme (FP10), coordinated by the ANR-funded French partner; this raises the caps to 200 000 EUR, 270 000 EUR and 370 000 EUR respectively.
Only the eligible costs of the partners that have requested ANR aid are financed; the applicable funding rate and cost types are set by the ANR Financial Regulation (eligible costs sheet no. 3).

Partners of selected projects are funded directly by their respective national/regional organisations (agencies or ministries); this is institutional research funding rather than a personal scholarship, and no tuition, living-cost or travel allowance is established for individuals.
application_method: Deposit is centralised in two steps on the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission site; pre-proposals and proposals, written in English, are deposited by the project coordinator in the format and modalities requested on the call site.
Step 1 (closed): the pre-proposal had to be deposited by 12/05/2026 at 12:00 CEST; the ANR does not require a deposit on its site at step 1.
Step 2 (open): only coordinators selected at the end of step 1 may deposit a detailed proposal, by 18/11/2026 at 12:00 CET.

Proposals with at least one partner requesting ANR aid invited to step 2 must in addition deposit their detailed proposal on the ANR submission site, with information identical to the central deposit; the exact link and deadline are communicated directly to candidates by email.

Any change must be communicated to and accepted by the requested funding agencies and the call secretariat at least two weeks before the step 2 closing date, with the consortium coordinator ensuring acceptance.
The call secretariat (office@m-era.net) is the point of contact for any candidate throughout the process.
official.application_route: Two-step central submission by the project coordinator on the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission site; ANR-funded partners additionally deposit the identical detailed proposal on the ANR submission site once emailed the exact link and deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: Aid is requested from and paid by each partner's own national or regional organisation; ANR aid is open to French partners within the consortium, whose participation the ANR expects to be significant (in coordination or in charge of a substantial part of the research work).
official.international_eligibility: International participation is mandatory: the consortium must include at least three funded partners from at least three different countries, of which at least two are EU Member States or Horizon Europe associated countries participating in the M-ERA.NET Call 2026.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Only one scientific collaboration theme may be addressed per proposal; for ANR funding only themes 1 (materials for energy storage and distribution systems), 2 (materials for energy conversion), 4 (innovative functional materials with designed architectures) and 6 (next-generation materials for electronics) are eligible, and the relevance to the chosen theme must be clearly justified from step 1.
official.research_requirement: Research projects only, funded on actual costs under the ANR Financial Regulation; work by partners requesting ANR aid must be positioned in the 'fundamental research' segment or the first 'applied research' segment, with an end-of-project TRL not exceeding 5 for an ANR-funded partner.
official.duration: Maximum project duration is 3 years (36 months).
official.description: More than 30 funding agencies participate in the M-ERA.NET 2026 call (2027 edition for the ANR) to fund ambitious transnational R&D projects in materials research and innovation, supporting the European Green Deal and the UN Sustainable Development Goals. The call is structured around 6 themes, of which 4 are eligible for the ANR, and the M-ERA.NET consortium, active since 2012, has federated a vast network in materials enabling collaboration between the leading academic and industrial research partners of European and non-European countries and regions. Supported projects have fostered the production of knowledge ranging from fundamental research to innovative industrial applications.
official.region: Europe (transnational, European and non-European countries and regions)
official.program_type: Transnational research project funding call (ERA-NET), research grant
official.english_requirement: Pre-proposals and detailed proposals, as well as Annex 1, must be written in English; the ANR also states that a translation of the evaluation criteria may be provided on request.

not_confirmed: study_mode (not published for this consortium research funding call)
person-month balance thresholds between partners and countries (published in the M-ERA.NET Guide for Proposers PDF, which was unreachable at verification time)
living_cost_coverage, travel_coverage and tuition_coverage for individuals (the ANR publishes only the eligible research costs of funded partners; no individual allowance is established)
verification.notes: Funding caps (no aid below 15 000 EUR per partner, 180 000 / 250 000 EUR partner ceilings, 350 000 EUR project ceiling, 20 000 EUR network supplement raising ceilings to 200 / 270 / 370 000 EUR), the TRL ceiling of 5, ANR-eligible themes 1/2/4/6 and the 18/11/2026 step-2 deadline were all read directly from the ANR annex PDF and the ANR call page; the M-ERA.NET call page confirmed the open full-proposal phase, 35 participating funding agencies and an indicative budget of about 40 million EUR.

applicant_utility.summary: This is institutional research funding for consortia, not a personal scholarship: ANR aid is paid to each partner's own national or regional organisation, so no individual student can apply on their own. A French organisation must sit inside a consortium of at least three funded partners from three different countries and route the bid through its own research administration. If your pre-proposal was recommended by three or more funding agencies, the binding date is 18 November 2026 at 12:00 CET, and any partner asking for ANR money must also file the identical detailed proposal on the ANR submission site once the agency emails the link.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A French research organisation or company already inside an invited M-ERA.NET consortium that needs 15,000-250,000 EUR of ANR co-funding for a materials project whose end TRL stays at or below 5.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm with your institution's research office that the ANR-specific national rules are satisfiable before drafting work packages: theme match, TRL ceiling, and significant French participation.

Budget every French partner inside the caps (180 000 EUR non-coordinator, 250 000 EUR coordinator, 350 000 EUR for a multi-partner ANR project) from step 1, because requested amounts cannot be increased at step 2.
Secure the scientific lead's formal commitment early: the ANR requires written confirmation that administrative and financial services approved the submission.
Contact your institution's defence and security officer or PPST service before any deposit if foreign public or private partners are involved, since a negative opinion blocks selection outright.
Collect CVs for every consortium participant, not only work-package leaders, because Annex 1 must profile all partners and all participants.
Work from the unmodified M-ERA.NET templates and respect page limits; unauthorised edits are treated as an inequity between participants and can void the bid.
common_rejection_risks: Theme mismatch: anything under theme 3 (innovative surfaces, coatings and interfaces) or theme 5 (materials addressing environmental challenges) can never receive ANR aid, so French partners in such consortia can only join on own funds.
TRL breach: an end-of-project TRL above 5 for an ANR-funded partner, or work drifting past the first applied-research segment, makes that partner ineligible.

Consortium imbalance: a single partner holding more than 60% or a single country more than 70% of total person-months, or losing 15% or more of effort when ineligible partners drop, discards the entire proposal.
Inconsistent or missing second deposit: ANR-funded partners must file the identical detailed proposal on the ANR site; divergence between the two deposits undermines the funding request.
Near-duplicate proposals: a proposal whose main objectives are identical to, or a simple adaptation of, another ANR proposal under evaluation or already funded is ruled out.

Sanctioned partners: an ANR partner associated with a partner covered by EU sanctions (as published, Russia and Belarus, and territories of Ukraine outside Ukrainian government control) is declared ineligible.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The ANR finances only the eligible costs of the partners requesting its aid under the ANR Financial Regulation; ineligible cost categories, overheads outside the funding rate, and any partner not requesting ANR aid must be carried by that partner's own institution or its national agency.
document_audit: Annex 1 with the CVs of all consortium participants is the item most often assembled too late; start gathering CVs the moment the step-2 invitation arrives.
The two deposits (M-ERA.NET central and ANR) must be scientifically and technically identical; keep one controlled master document and compare it field by field before submitting.

The consortium agreement and the Data Management Plan (due within 6 months of the scientific start) are post-award obligations that must already be planned into governance and budget at proposal stage.

The 'Declaration relative aux activites economiques des Partenaires' form sets the applicable funding rate and eligible cost types, so a mis-declared economic activity can silently change the aid actually available.
alerts: Step 1 closed on 12 May 2026 at 12:00 CEST; the only remaining entry point this cycle is step 2, and only for coordinators already invited by M-ERA.NET.
Requested amounts may not be increased between the two steps, so an under-budgeted step 1 cannot be corrected in November.

New partners cannot be added from countries not already present at step 1, and any consortium change must be accepted by the funding agencies and the secretariat at least two weeks before 18 November 2026.

Proposals may be transmitted to other administrations, control bodies and partner funders, and some national funders publish submitted proposals, so keep intellectual-property and business-secret content out of the forms.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: The coordinator submits on the M-ERA.NET submission tool, then ANR-funded partners file the identical detailed proposal on the ANR submission site once the agency sends the exact link and deadline by email.
